summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology focused on robotics software systems and perception. Built real-time computer vision and machine learning pipelines on NVIDIA Jetson hardware, optimizing inference with GPGPU (CUDA) and TensorRT for robotic perception. Proficient in C/C++/Python across embedded, perception, and Linux-based robotics systems.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Trained a YOLOv3 computer vision model from scratch for real-time ball detection, driving closed-loop visual servoing motor commands for a competition robot's robotics software system.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and machine learning algorithms integration end-to-end.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a vision-guided robotic pick-and-place robotics software system over a three-layer distributed pipeline (mobile client, edge server, Jetson+Arduino controller).
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO computer vision (5.2x speedup, 56.7->10.9ms, 17.6->92 FPS) for real-time visual servoing and dual ToF sensors for contact-aware grasping.

Deployed the Jetson-side robotics software as a Linux systemd service, troubleshooting 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) to reach 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 computer vision on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART for a closed-loop robotics software system.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and FreeRTOS task coordination; integrated ToF sensing for distance-aware tracking.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Built automated dynamic-simulation data-generation pipelines using semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering, producing ~5,000 computer vision training frames with zero manual annotation.

Trained and fine-tuned object-detection and lane-following models integrated into an adaptive control stack; validated in simulation with 30 vehicles and 10 pedestrians, achieving zero collisions across multiple laps.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript convolution layers with custom GPGPU (CUDA) C++ kernels using memory coalescing and constant memory, achieving a 1.5-2x speedup with identical classification accuracy.
Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms vs 73.3ms uncoalesced and 77.5ms CPU baseline — ~35% speedup through efficient global memory utilization.
